metrics.label: Races
metrics.desc: Grand Prix starts in the season (entries that did not start are not counted).

metrics.label: Wins
metrics.desc: Grand Prix wins.

metrics.label: Podiums
metrics.desc: Top-three Grand Prix finishes.

metrics.label: Win rate
metrics.desc: Wins divided by starts.

metrics.label: Podium rate
metrics.desc: Podiums divided by starts.

metrics.label: Top-5 rate
metrics.desc: Top-five finishes divided by starts.

metrics.label: Average finish
metrics.desc: Mean finishing position over the races the driver was classified in. Retirements are left out, so read it with the DNF rate. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Median finish
metrics.desc: Median finishing position over classified finishes; less pulled about by one bad afternoon than the mean. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Best finish
metrics.desc: Best finishing position of the season.

metrics.label: Average grid
metrics.desc: Mean starting slot. A pit-lane start counts as the last slot. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Laps led
metrics.desc: Laps completed in the lead (first across the line at the end of the lap), from lap-by-lap positions.

metrics.label: Share of laps led
metrics.desc: Laps led as a share of the laps the driver completed.

metrics.label: Race head-to-head v team-mate
metrics.desc: Share of races the driver finished ahead of the team-mate. Counted when at least one of them was classified; a retirement loses to a finish.

metrics.label: Fastest laps
metrics.desc: Races in which the driver set the fastest lap.

metrics.label: Average fastest-lap rank
metrics.desc: Mean rank of the driver's fastest lap in each race (1 = the race's fastest lap). A raw-speed signal that ignores fuel and tyres. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Field Elo (season end)
metrics.desc: Field Elo after the driver's last race of the season: a rating of the finishing order against the whole field, so it rates driver plus car. 1500 is average.

metrics.label: Team-mate Elo (season end)
metrics.desc: Team-mate Elo after the driver's last race of the season: updated only on head-to-heads with team-mates (same car), the cleaner driver rating. 1500 is average.

metrics.label: Poles
metrics.desc: Qualifying sessions topped (before grid penalties).

metrics.label: Front-row rate
metrics.desc: Share of qualifying sessions finished first or second.

metrics.label: Q3 rate
metrics.desc: Share of qualifying sessions in which the driver reached Q3 (2006 onwards).

metrics.label: Q1 exit rate
metrics.desc: Share of qualifying sessions in which the driver was knocked out in Q1 (2006 onwards). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Average qualifying position
metrics.desc: Mean qualifying position. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Gap to pole (%)
metrics.desc: Gap to the pole-sitter in percent of the lap: 100 x (driver's time / pole time - 1), compared in the deepest segment the driver set a time in (Q3, else Q2, else Q1) so both laps were run on the same track. Season value is the median. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Gap to team-mate (ms)
metrics.desc: Gap to the team-mate in qualifying, in milliseconds: driver's time minus team-mate's time in the deepest segment both set a time in. Negative means faster. Season value is the median over the weekends. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Gap to team-mate (%)
metrics.desc: The team-mate gap in percent of the lap: 100 x (driver's time / team-mate's time - 1), median over the season. Negative means faster. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Qualifying head-to-head v team-mate
metrics.desc: Share of qualifying sessions in which the driver out-qualified the team-mate (by classification).

metrics.label: Qualifying pace (% v field)
metrics.desc: Corrected one-lap pace in percent of the lap against the field mean: every driver's Q1/Q2/Q3 times become gaps to each segment's fastest time and a segment offset is removed, so drivers knocked out early are compared fairly. Negative is faster. Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Qualifying pace rank
metrics.desc: Rank of the driver's corrected qualifying pace in each session (1 = fastest). Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Qualifying driver effect (%)
metrics.desc: The driver part of the season's qualifying-pace decomposition: how much faster (negative) or slower than the team-mate(s) the driver was over one lap, in percent of the lap, shrunk toward zero when the evidence is thin. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Grid drop (penalties)
metrics.desc: Mean starting slot minus qualifying position: places lost to grid penalties (or gained from others' penalties). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Race pace (s/lap v field)
metrics.desc: Corrected race pace in seconds per lap against the field mean, from the lap-time model: each clean lap is explained by car and driver, fuel load, tyre compound and age, track evolution and traffic, and the car-plus-driver term is the pace. Negative is faster. Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Race pace (% v field)
metrics.desc: Corrected race pace in percent of the reference (median clean) lap. Negative is faster. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Race pace rank (mean)
metrics.desc: Rank of the driver's corrected race pace in each race (1 = fastest). Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Season race-pace rank
metrics.desc: Rank of the driver's season-mean race pace among drivers with a pace in at least a third of the races (1 = fastest).

metrics.label: Best race-pace rank
metrics.desc: Best single-race pace rank of the season.

metrics.label: Race pace v team-mate (s/lap)
metrics.desc: Race pace minus the team-mate's race pace in the same race, seconds per lap. Negative means quicker than the team-mate in the same car. Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Race pace head-to-head v team-mate
metrics.desc: Share of races in which the driver's corrected race pace beat the team-mate's.

metrics.label: Race driver effect (%)
metrics.desc: The driver part of the season's race-pace decomposition: pace relative to the team-mate(s) in percent of the lap, after the car's round-by-round level is taken out, shrunk toward zero. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Lap-time scatter (s)
metrics.desc: Lap-time scatter: standard deviation of the driver's clean laps after removing the fitted fuel and tyre-wear effects, in seconds. Smaller means metronomic. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Time lost in traffic (s/race)
metrics.desc: Seconds per race the lap-time model attributes to running in dirty air (within 1.5 s of the car ahead at the start of a lap). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Wet-race pace rank
metrics.desc: Mean race-pace rank in races flagged wet (rain in at least 10% of the race's weather samples, or a quarter of the field on intermediates or wets). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Sector strength (share of PB sectors that were session-best)
metrics.desc: Sector strength: of the driver's personal-best sector times in each race and qualifying session, the share that were the fastest of the session.

metrics.label: Personal-best sector rank
metrics.desc: Mean rank of the driver's personal-best sector times among the session's drivers (1 = the session's best). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Positions gained
metrics.desc: Grid slot minus finishing position, over classified finishes. Positive means places gained. Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured.

metrics.label: Lap-1 gain
metrics.desc: Grid slot minus running position at the end of lap 1: the start and first lap. Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured.

metrics.label: Gain after lap 1
metrics.desc: Positions gained after lap 1: positions gained minus the lap-1 gain.

metrics.label: Overtakes made per race
metrics.desc: On-track passes made per race (OpenF1's overtakes, with position changes caused by a pit stop removed).

metrics.label: Overtakes suffered per race
metrics.desc: Times the driver was passed on track per race. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Net overtakes per race
metrics.desc: Overtakes made minus overtakes suffered, per race.

metrics.label: Pass difficulty (s/lap)
metrics.desc: Mean pace deficit on the passes the driver made: the overtaker's corrected race pace minus the overtaken car's, seconds per lap. Positive means the driver passed cars that were faster on the day.

metrics.label: Overtakes per unit pace deficit
metrics.desc: Overtakes per unit pace deficit: overtakes made per race divided by (0.25 s + the mean pace advantage the driver had over the cars passed, floored at zero). High when a driver passes a lot without a big pace advantage.

metrics.label: Penalties
metrics.desc: Penalties handed down by the stewards in the race and sprint, counted from race-control notices that name the driver's car (served-penalty and no-further-action notices excluded). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Penalties per race
metrics.desc: Penalties per race. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Degradation: soft (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Tyre degradation on the soft compound: seconds per lap lost for every lap of tyre age, from the lap-time model (fuel burn removed). Season value is the mean over the races where it can be measured. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Degradation: medium (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Tyre degradation on the medium compound, seconds per lap per lap of age. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Degradation: hard (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Tyre degradation on the hard compound, seconds per lap per lap of age. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Tyre management index
metrics.desc: Tyre management index: minus 1000 x the mean gap between the driver's degradation and the field median on the same compound in the same race, in milliseconds per lap per lap of age. Positive means the driver's tyres fell away more slowly than the field's.

metrics.label: Stint length v field (laps)
metrics.desc: Mean stint length minus the field's median stint on the same compound in the same race, in laps. Positive means longer stints. A final stint cut short by a retirement is left out.

metrics.label: Average stint (laps)
metrics.desc: Mean stint length in laps.

metrics.label: Stops per race
metrics.desc: Pit stops per race started. Fewer stops for the same result usually means kinder tyre use, so lower ranks higher.

metrics.label: Pit-lane time (median)
metrics.desc: Median time from pit entry to pit exit for the driver's stops. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Finish rate
metrics.desc: Share of starts that ended classified.

metrics.label: DNF rate
metrics.desc: Share of starts that ended unclassified (retired, or disqualified). Lower is better.

metrics.label: DNFs: driver-caused
metrics.desc: Retirements the status records as driver-caused: accident, collision, spun off. Lower is better.

metrics.label: DNFs: mechanical
metrics.desc: Retirements the status records as mechanical: engine, gearbox, hydraulics and so on. Lower is better.

metrics.label: DNFs: cause not published
metrics.desc: Retirements with no published cause (recent seasons only publish 'Retired') and disqualifications. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Did not start
metrics.desc: Entries that did not start. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Share of race laps completed
metrics.desc: Laps completed as a share of the race distances of the races started.

metrics.label: Expected points lost in DNFs
metrics.desc: Expected points (from the forecast at lights-out) in the races the driver did not finish: what the retirements were worth. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Braking-point earliness v field (m)
metrics.desc: Braking-point earliness: for each corner, how far before the apex the driver starts braking (median over the driver's laps) minus the field median, averaged over corners, in metres. Negative means later braking than the field.

metrics.label: Minimum corner speed v field (km/h)
metrics.desc: Minimum corner speed against the field: the driver's median slowest speed through each corner minus the field median, averaged over corners, km/h. Positive means more speed carried.

metrics.label: Full throttle (% of lap)
metrics.desc: Share of the lap spent at full throttle (98% or more), median over the driver's laps.

metrics.label: Braking (% of lap)
metrics.desc: Share of the lap spent on the brakes, median over the driver's laps.

metrics.label: Coasting (% of lap)
metrics.desc: Share of the lap spent coasting (off the throttle and off the brakes), median over the driver's laps. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Speed trap (km/h)
metrics.desc: Top speed-trap reading per session (race and qualifying), averaged over the season, km/h.

metrics.label: Speed-trap rank
metrics.desc: Rank of the driver's top speed-trap reading in each session (1 = fastest), averaged. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Points
metrics.desc: Championship points as awarded (Grand Prix, sprint and fastest-lap points), before any dropped-score rule.

metrics.label: Points per race
metrics.desc: Points divided by starts.

metrics.label: Points-finish rate
metrics.desc: Share of starts that scored points.

metrics.label: Share of team points
metrics.desc: The driver's share of the team's points in the season.

metrics.label: Championship position
metrics.desc: Position in the drivers' championship. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Expected points
metrics.desc: Expected points: the sum of the walk-forward forecast's expected points at lights-out (post-qualifying), race by race.

metrics.label: Points v expected
metrics.desc: Points minus expected points (post-qualifying forecast), summed over the season: points scored beyond what the car, grid slot and form predicted.

metrics.label: Points v expected (pre-qualifying)
metrics.desc: Points minus the pre-qualifying forecast's expected points: like points v expected, but also credits qualifying.

metrics.label: Sprint points
metrics.desc: Points from sprint races.

metrics.label: Sprint positions gained
metrics.desc: Sprint grid slot minus sprint finishing position, over classified sprint finishes.

peer_rule: Race drivers with at least `peer_floor` starts: 8 in a finished season of 16+ rounds, else max(3, min(8, ceil(0.35 x rounds completed))); drivers below it get no peer percentile and are nobody's similar driver.
similar_method: The 5 nearest driver-seasons from 1996 on (the driver's own seasons excluded) by weighted Euclidean distance on the eight headline metrics (race and qualifying driver ratings, race head-to-head, share of team points, race pace, points per race, team-mate Elo, lap-1 gain), each z-scored within its season among the qualifying drivers and weighted by its season-to-season reliability (floored at 0.2); a feature missing for either season is dropped (at least 6 of 8 must remain). d is in standard deviations.
